Property Overview

30+ Acres Above Boulder. Infrastructure In. Plans Approved.

This is a vacant land listing, and that’s what makes it worth paying attention to. For $350,000 you’re not buying raw dirt — you’re buying ~30.72 acres of ridge-top Boulder County mountain land with a producing well, an installed septic system, electric service at the property, and a final Boulder County Site Plan Review (SPR) approval for a luxury residence already in hand. The hard, expensive, slow groundwork is done.

The backstory matters here: a wildfire tore through this property more than a decade ago, which is why the land looks the way it does in the photos — open, rolling, with the remnants of burned timber still visible across the slopes. That fire also cleared the prior improvements and allowed the current owner to start fresh. The well, septic, and utility infrastructure you see today were installed as part of that rebuild process. The open, post-fire landscape is actually one of the reasons the views are so extraordinary — 360 degrees of unobstructed panorama from snow-capped peaks to the city lights of Boulder below.

The seller is also carrying a companion listing at $1,442,322 for the full build-out of a designed luxury home on this same parcel. That path is real and worth understanding, but Chelsea’s interest is in the land itself — what comes with it, what transfers, and what she could do from here with her own vision and team. That’s what this report focuses on.

📋 Note on approved square footage: The land listing remarks reference approved plans for a 2,138 SF residence. The companion build-out listing and the Boulder County SPR record both reference a 3,780 SF structure on the same parcel. I’ve asked the listing agent to clarify — the SPR determination letter will be the controlling document. This is a key open item before any offer.

Boulder County Planning

Site Plan Review — SPR-22-0103

Boulder County requires a Site Plan Review for mountain residential development that exceeds size thresholds or is in sensitive areas. This is not a rubber stamp — the process involved formal referrals to more than a dozen agencies and resulted in a written determination with conditions of approval. That approval is on record and in a land purchase scenario, it’s one of the most valuable things transferring with the deed.

Agent’s Take

Here’s What I’m Seeing

My Analysis · Zachary Springborn · JPAR® Modern Real Estate

Chelsea, starting with the land is the right instinct. At $350,000 for ~31 acres above Boulder with a well, septic, utilities, and a county-approved entitlement, you’re paying for a very real set of improvements that took years and significant money to put in place. The fire that swept through here over a decade ago is actually part of why this opportunity exists — it reset the land, forced new infrastructure, and left behind an open ridge-top site with views that most properties in Boulder County simply cannot offer.

The SF discrepancy between the land listing (2,138 SF) and the SPR record and build-out listing (3,780 SF) is the thing I’m most focused on right now. It’s possible the 2,138 SF figure in the remarks is an older or different plan, and the SPR was later revised upward. Or it could be a marketing error. Either way, the SPR determination letter resolves it and I’ve asked for it. That document also tells us whether there are wildfire mitigation conditions, road improvements required, or any other obligations that would pass to a new owner — those are all things you’d inherit with the land.

The road is worth a specific conversation. Private dirt road, not to county standards, with a road association in place — that’s typical for this area but the details matter. I want to see what the association agreement looks like, what the annual maintenance cost-share is, and whether there are any known access issues in winter. That’s not a dealbreaker, but it’s a real ongoing ownership cost that needs to be understood before you’re under contract.

I’ve sent the due diligence questions to the listing agent and am waiting to hear back. Once I have the SPR letter, the well data, the septic details, and the road association docs in hand I’ll update this report and we can have a real conversation about next steps.

Balanced View

Strengths & Considerations

✅ Strengths
  • $350,000 for ~31 acres with infrastructure already in — significant value relative to raw land
  • 360° panoramic views — peaks, foothills, plains, and Boulder city lights
  • Well (permit #166491), septic, and electric already on-site — each representing years and substantial cost to install in this terrain
  • Boulder County SPR final approval in hand — entitlement is exceptionally hard to obtain above the presumptive size maximum
  • Post-fire land is open, accessible, and regenerating — fire history is also why views are unobstructed
  • No HOA, no metro district — low encumbrance ownership
  • Horse property — horses allowed
  • Minimal flood risk
  • If plans transfer, Chelsea would inherit a county-approved design she can use or modify as the basis for her own build
⚠️ Considerations
  • SF discrepancy between land listing (2,138 SF) and SPR/build-out listing (3,780 SF) is unresolved — open item
  • SPR determination letter and conditions of approval not yet in hand — may include material obligations
  • Private dirt road, not to county standards — road association details, year-round access, and maintenance costs are TBD
  • Well flow rate and water quality test results not yet confirmed
  • Electric service: permanent vs. temporary hookup not confirmed
  • Wildfire / WUI zone — Gold Hill area has significant fire history; insurance must be independently verified
  • 70 days on market — explore seller motivation
  • Taxes ($11,875/yr) are based on current unimproved value; will increase significantly once home is built and assessed
  • Cash or conventional only — land financing can be complex; lender selection matters

Wildfire & WUI Disclosure

This property is located in the Gold Hill area of Boulder County, which has Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) designations and a documented wildfire history. Buyers must independently verify wildfire hazard designations, insurance availability and cost, defensible space requirements, and any mitigation conditions in the SPR determination prior to purchase.

Well & Septic Advisory

This property is served by a private well and on-site septic system. Independent well flow rate, water quality, and potability testing, as well as septic inspection and capacity assessment, are required prior to purchase.

Road Access Advisory

Access via a private road not maintained to Boulder County standards. Buyers must independently evaluate year-round accessibility, road association obligations, and maintenance cost-sharing prior to purchase.

Land & New Construction Advisory

This report covers a vacant land listing. Any future construction is subject to Boulder County SPR conditions, building permit requirements, and applicable regulations at time of permit application. Approved plans and entitlements should be independently verified by a licensed architect or land use attorney prior to purchase.
